title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
abstract: arXiv:2611.08392v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings,

translated_title: 学习用于重症监护医疗系统模拟的患者世界模型
translated_abstract: 设计医疗策略需要在实施之前预测其临床和运营层面的后果，这一任务通常依赖于医疗系统模拟。这样的模拟需要对患者状态如何演化并产生医疗需求进行建模。然而，传统方法通常针对单一政策问题定制紧凑的状态转移模型，并忽略了依赖于历史的动态特性，因此当出现需要不同临床信息的新问题时，就必须重新定义状态和转移。我们提出利用神经网络从纵向电子健康记录（EHR）中学习一个患者世界模型，为患者轨迹提供一个共享的临床表示，从而可以服务于跨多种场景的模拟问题。以ICU运营为例，我们在MIMIC-IV数据集上训练该模型并将其冻结，随后通过针对特定场景的映射，将其可按时间查询的预测结果与共享的ICU日历、资源和队列相耦合。
tldr: 该论文提出从纵向电子健康记录中学习一个患者世界模型，为重症监护医疗系统模拟提供可跨多种场景复用的患者轨迹共享临床表示，避免了为每个新问题重新定义状态和转移模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes learning a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs, providing a shared, reusable clinical representation of patient trajectories for health system simulation in intensive care, thus avoiding the need to redefine states and transitions for each new policy question.
